bull_bear.body:
- Zero Debt policy — the Company states it would like to expand on internal accruals and revenue rather than borrowings
- Land inventory safeguarded in both Bengaluru and Chennai, held awaiting the right opportunity to invest and construct commercial properties
- Single-segment real estate focus with a wholly-owned NBFC subsidiary providing a second (financial) income stream
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Economic and cyclical exposure of a single real-estate business — The MD&A states that an economic slowdown or recession in a specific industry such as IT/ITES can decrease sales or market rates for residential projects, and that in an extreme downturn the Company may face customer insolvency; a real estate company's business in India is dependent on the easy availability of finance, and a slowdown can cause fund shortages as lenders act safe.
- Liquidity risk on illiquid property assets — Management notes the time required to liquidate a real estate property varies with the size, volume, demand, quality and location of the project — the Company's value sits in land inventory that cannot be turned into cash quickly.
- Credit and counterparty risk on joint-venture partners and buyers — Most properties are on a joint venture / sale basis; if JV partners or buyers do not discharge their obligations, the Company may have to make additional investments in a joint venture or become liable for the other party's obligations. This is structural given the Company's stated strategy of developing land through JVs.
- Regulatory and approval risk over land use and construction — Local, state and central bodies control acquisition, construction and development of land through zoning, permitted land use, fire safety, building height and utility access rules; any delay in obtaining an approval exposes the business to higher risk. The challenges section separately flags land acquisition complexities, delayed environmental clearances and slower municipal approvals causing project delays and execution risk.
- Legal risk on land title and taxation matters — The MD&A states that in some legal proceedings relating to land and to taxation matters, any adverse decision may have a significant effect on the Company's business, prospects and financials.
- Political and policy risk — Changes in government policy, social and civil unrest and political developments in or affecting India could affect the Company's business interests; specific laws and policies affecting real estate, foreign investment and investments in the Company's securities could also change.
- Affordability and interest-rate pressure on end demand — Global economic volatility and elevated domestic interest rates have impacted homebuyer affordability and raised the cost of capital for developers, with housing prices rising faster than incomes, so affordability constraints are visible in the mid-income and affordable segments.
- Geographic and single-segment concentration — The Company is engaged only in the business of real estate activities with no other reportable segment, and its land inventory is concentrated in Chennai and Bengaluru; management states the strategy of focusing real estate activity for various geographical segments is exposed to economic and fluctuating market conditions.

business.body: The Company operates in only one segment, the real estate business, and holds land and buildings as stock-in-trade for property development. Its revenue arises from rentals of the Company's properties invoiced as fixed monthly charges or on a time-proportionate basis, from real-estate contract cancellations in the usual course of the real estate business, and from interest and dividend income. Its subsidiary, S V Global Finance Private Limited, operates as a non-deposit-taking NBFC.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no named capex project, no commissioning timeline and no rupee capex quantum. Expansion intent is stated only as land-bank optionality: the Company says it has diligently safeguarded its inventories in the form of lands in both Bengaluru and Chennai, waiting for the rightful opportunity to invest, construct commercial properties, expand and optimise returns to stakeholders. It states a Zero Debt policy and that it would like to expand on internal accruals and revenue. It is constantly evaluating joint-venture development for housing or commercial buildings, while for parcels not ideal for JV development it is weighing leasing the land for exhibitions and car parking and seeking suitable buyers to dispose of them. Management adds that it is constantly looking for suitable avenues to identify and venture into new projects and business opportunities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Real estate accounts for 7.3% of India's GDP and remains central to the growth trajectory, with growing project scale, cost pressures and tighter regulatory oversight pushing developers towards digital and data-driven execution tools
- The Indian real estate sector is in a phase of stabilisation and moderation in FY 2025-26 after a decade of robust growth, with new project launches down 17 to 18% as developers act cautiously to prevent oversupply
- A controlled cool-down in volumes with sales dipping in eight major cities, yet total market value rising on a per-square-foot increase of up to 8% at the national level; real estate prices are expected to increase 5 to 7% annually
- Luxury and premium housing (above Rs 1 crore) continues to drive demand while affordable housing faces pressure
- Government support for affordable housing through PMAY-Urban and PMAY-Urban 2.0 (outlay of Rs 21,625 crores, targeting 1 crore additional houses between 2024-2029) and SWAMIH 2.0 (planned corpus of Rs 15,000 crores)
- Urbanisation and infrastructure development sustain demand, channelled through Bharatmala Pariyojana, Sagarmala, Smart Cities Mission and UDAN, with Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities above 5 lakh population prioritised
- Office demand is set to stabilise at 70-75 million square feet with Global Capability Centres driving growth, and data centres are expected to grow rapidly by 2027
- Investment need is shifting towards commercial space, logistics and warehousing, evidenced by a spurt in metro commercial rentals taken by the world's top companies and by start-ups and unicorns
- Macro backdrop: RBI projects FY 2026-27 GDP growth at 6.9% versus 7.6% for FY 2025-26, with quarterly estimates trimmed on global headwinds and rising energy prices; headline inflation averaged about 2.1% in FY 2025-26
- Elevated domestic interest rates and housing prices rising faster than incomes are constraining affordability in the mid-income and affordable segments
